caption_used: Massive activation values across layers under baseline conditions, showing four component signals. The ffn_residual (red solid) and attn_residual (orange dotted) lines rise sharply at layer 5 to approximately 1400, with ffn_residual maintaining values between 1400 and 1600 through layer 20 before declining. The attn_residual closely mirrors ffn_residual but with a one-layer rightward shift. The ffn_output (green dash-dot) exhibits periodic spikes at layers 5, 13, and 22, reaching peak values of approximately 800. The attn_output (blue dashed) remains near zero throughout all layers, with no notable increase at any point in the network. The data indicates that massive activations in the baseline are driven primarily by the feed-forward network residual stream, with attention outputs contributing negligibly.

raw_responses.Bulgarian: DESCRIPTION: The figure illustrates the maximum activation values across layers for four different components in a neural network under baseline conditions, with the x-axis representing the layer number and the y-axis representing the maximum activation value. The x-axis ranges from 0 to 22, with integer labels at intervals of 5, and the y-axis ranges from 0 to 1600, with labels at intervals of 200. The "ffn_residual" (red solid line) begins at 0 at layer 0, rises sharply to approximately 1400 at layer 5, remains between 1400 and 1600 through layer 20, and then declines to approximately 600 at layer 22. The "attn_residual" (orange dotted line) follows a similar trend but is shifted one layer to the right, starting at 0 at layer 0, rising to approximately 1400 at layer 6, and maintaining values between 1400 and 1600 through layer 21 before declining. The "ffn_output" (green dash-dot line) remains near 0 until layer 5, where it spikes to approximately 800, returns to near 0, spikes again to approximately 800 at layer 13, and then spikes once more to approximately 800 at layer 22. The "attn_output" (blue dashed line) remains near 0 across all layers, with no significant increase observed at any point.
